content:
The image shows a bunch of green bananas (fruit/pod stage) with distinctive symptoms:

- **Affected part**: Fruit (banana fingers/hands)
- **Key visual features**:
  - Dark brown/black necrotic tissue at the **tips** of the banana fingers (blossom end)
  - The rot appears dry and mummified at the distal end of each fruit
  - The necrosis starts at the flower-end tip and works inward
  - The fruit body remains green and otherwise intact
  - The withered, shriveled dark material at tips resembles a "cigar" burnt end

This pattern — dry, dark necrosis confined to the tip/blossom end of banana fruits, giving a cigar-like burnt appearance — is the hallmark of **Cigar End Rot**, caused by *Verticillium theobromae* or *Trachysphaera fructigena*. The disease infects through the persistent flower parts at the fruit tip, causing this characteristic tip necrosis.
